subject: open-interpreter
title: Apache-2.0 compliant rebrand, but residual provenance/trademark exposure
evidence: diff -q codex/LICENSE open-interpreter/LICENSE clean; codex-rs/product-info/src/lib.rs:12-32 (openai/codex release URLs, chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh shipped as CODEX_* fallbacks)
one_why: No copyright violation - LICENSE and NOTICE are byte-identical to upstream - but the product still carries codex-branded prompt assets and install URLs behind a rival identity; risk is trademark and provenance confusion, not infringement. Study-integrity finding: census 'rename-clone' overstates the legal exposure here.

subject: open-interpreter
title: root package.json never renamed - defeats provenance tooling and census detection
one_why: Deliberate choice ('do not globally replace codex') is defensible internally but makes every downstream tooling pass (our census, license scanners, supply-chain audits) misclassify the repo; a single product-manifest field would fix it. Convergence with mimo-code-2.

subject: open-interpreter
title: centralized product-identity crate makes rebrand testable instead of search-and-replace
one_why: All user-facing names/URLs route through Product::current(); there is a test asserting product identity - the clean way to keep a long-lived fork mergeable, worth stealing if we ever brand a distribution.

subject: open-interpreter
title: fork work concentrates in transport/provider plane, not the loop
one_why: Shows what a low-cost-model-focused fork actually changes vs an S-grade upstream: Anthropic wire compat, model catalogs, harness selection, ACP surface - the agent loop itself is left untouched.
